scope: Legend/belief/dog topics where claim classification matters.

topics.title: Giếng Tiên

claims.claim: The Phú Quốc government portal describes Giếng Tiên as a freshwater spring emerging from rock in the An Thới area, later enclosed by a small wall for collecting water.
The same official page places Giếng Tiên roughly 2 km from An Thới.
The story that Nguyễn Ánh struck/cut into rock and freshwater appeared, while anchovies came from the sea to sustain his men, is explicitly introduced by the local government page as a folk legend.
The tourism text says the small spring does not run dry despite water being taken. This should be treated as a local descriptive claim until hydrological or field evidence is found.

sources.title: Những giai thoại, truyền thuyết trên đảo ngọc Phú Quốc

known_unknowns: Exact coordinates and current public access route.
Documented historical evidence linking Nguyễn Ánh to this exact spring, distinct from later folklore.
next_research: Find old maps/archival records for Mũi Ông Đội and Giếng Tiên.
Field-verify access, coordinates and current condition.
Research Nguyễn Ánh's documented movements around Phú Quốc separately from the legend.

topics.title: Tín ngưỡng Dinh Cậu

claims.claim: Recent reporting and current tourism material describe Chúa Ngọc Nương Nương in the central/principal worship position, with Cậu Tài and Cậu Quý associated at Dinh Cậu.
Recent cultural reporting records that fishing was historically referred to locally as 'nghề Bà - Cậu', reflecting a protective belief system among fishing communities.
The exact original object(s) of worship and how the current altar arrangement developed over time remain contested across popular/local sources.
Current tourism sources place the Dinh Cậu festival on the 15th-16th days of the 10th lunar month.

sources.title: Dinh Cậu Phú Quốc: Tên Cậu nhưng giữa chánh điện lại là Bà?

known_unknowns: Primary historical records for the oldest form of worship at the site.
Precise relationship among Long Vương, Bà-Cậu, Chúa Ngọc Nương Nương, Cậu Tài and Cậu Quý in different periods.
Visitor etiquette and ritual practice that should be explained without turning belief into objective fact.
next_research: Locate cultural-history research and archival documents.
Separate present-day altar description from historical evolution.
Create a source-aware etiquette note for visitors.

topics.title: Chó Phú Quốc

claims.claim: The 2023 VKA breed standard states the origin as Phú Quốc Island, Vietnam.
The VKA standard identifies the reverse-growing ridge of hair along the back as a defining characteristic.
The VKA standard describes the breed's use as a hunting dog and emphasizes speed, agility and endurance.
The VKA standard says the breed is not afraid of heights or water and is capable of climbing and jumping very well.
The VKA standard uses an FCI-style group/subgroup classification. This alone is not evidence that FCI has definitively recognized Phú Quốc Ridgeback as an FCI breed.

sources.title: Bảng tiêu chuẩn giống chó Xoáy Phú Quốc số 001/VN/04.10.2023

known_unknowns: Current FCI recognition status needs explicit verification from FCI nomenclature, not inference from VKA group labels.
Genetic relationship to Thai Ridgeback/Rhodesian Ridgeback requires scientific sources.
Historical population and conservation status on the island.
next_research: Search FCI official nomenclature directly for recognition status.
Build an archive timeline from 19th-century European records cited by VKA.

topics.title: Chó Phú Quốc có thật sự leo cây?

claims.claim: The current VKA standard supports strong climbing and jumping ability, but does not specifically establish 'tree climbing' as a universal or diagnostic breed trait.

VKA-hosted historical/reporting material contains examples and local descriptions of Phú Quốc dogs climbing obstacles and being strong climbers; these support the origin of the popular claim but are not controlled evidence that the breed routinely climbs trees.
For Open Phu Quoc, 'chó Phú Quốc biết leo cây' should be presented as a curiosity claim with evidence levels, not as an unqualified biological fact.
